findings.description: [AI-SAST via Code Scan Verification Validation | claude-opus-5] Both build stages pin official Docker Hub python images by immutable sha256 digest rather than by mutable tag (line 6 builder, line 19 runtime), so a rebuild cannot silently pull an unreviewed base. Dependency installation at line 47 uses pip --require-hashes, which fails the whole build if any requirement lacks a hash, and the exported requirements come from a hash-bearing poetry export at line 16. No untrusted registry, no :latest and no unpinned tag reference remains | verdict=pass confidence=high

[AI-SAST via Code Scan Verification Validation | claude-opus-5] The lock file records each pinned digest alongside its intended tag and the date it was resolved (lines 19-20), and the header at lines 9-17 mandates the promotion procedure ctx.text asks for: resolve the new digest, run the image vulnerability scan, verify signature and provenance, update lock and Dockerfile in one reviewed commit, and refresh on a schedule so patches are not missed. This supplies the trusted-source, regular-update and image-scanning elements as a reviewed in-repo control | verdict=pass confidence=high

[AI-SAST via Code Scan Verification Validation | claude-opus-5] The lock file carries 1614 artifact hash entries across the resolved dependency set, so the requirements exported into the image are verified against fixed digests rather than against whatever the package index serves at build time; this is what makes the Dockerfile's --require-hashes install enforceable. No unhashed or unpinned dependency entry was observed | verdict=pass confidence=high

[AI-SAST via Code Scan Verification Validation | claude-opus-5] pip-audit is declared at line 75 in the dev group so the pinned dependency set is audited against the advisory database in CI and locally without shipping the tool into the image, and lines 30-55 pin explicit security floors for transitive packages (starlette, h11, urllib3, idna, anyio, click, mako, pyasn1, ecdsa, python-dotenv) so a future resolve cannot drop back onto a known-vulnerable release. Test and lint tooling was moved out of the runtime group, so it no longer reaches the production image | verdict=pass confidence=high
